claim: Rosa (J. Futures Markets 2022) tests the overnight-return variant of intraday momentum (overnight return predicts last half-hour) out of sample and finds predictability disappears out of sample; regime-dependent (Markov switching); thresholded strategy beats always-on. Not the first-half-hour variant.
quote: The predictability disappears in the out‐of‐sample period.
title: Rosa 2022, Understanding intraday momentum strategies

claim: CFR WP 26-02 (Bali, Goyal, Moerke, Weigert) is a seasonality paper: half-day option returns show momentum within same period and reversal across opposite periods, 0.22%-0.45% per half-day, persisting up to 20 business days, increasing over time; supply-side (market maker capacity). Data are delta-hedged option returns per its abstract; sample years (2004-2021 per search summary) not confirmed on cached page; not an option-buying rule with costs.
quote: These patterns increase over time, are robust to various delta-hedging schemes and option selection criteria, and persist across different subsamples.
title: In search of seasonality in intraday and overnight option returns

claim: QuantConnect recreation of the Stocks-in-Play ORB covered only 2016 (first year of paper sample), 1,000-stock universe: Sharpe 2.396 vs SPY 0.836; 17 of 25 parameter combinations beat benchmark; no post-2016 or post-publication test; no costs stated in the snippet.
quote: We backtested the algorithm during 2016, the first year of the paper's backtest period.
title: Opening Range Breakout for Stocks in Play (QuantConnect)

claim: QuantConnect forum users report backtest-vs-live gaps for the stocks-in-play ORB: in minute-resolution backtests the stop order is placed a minute after entry fill, unlike real time, so backtests overstate results; one user says fees matter and fills may be worse.
quote: This creates quite a difference between backtesting and live trading.
title: QuantConnect forum comments on stocks-in-play ORB

claim: Cboe (2023, vendor/exchange research): SPX 0DTE market-maker net gamma is small (0.04-0.17% of S&P futures daily volume) and the frequency of SPX intraday 2-sigma gap moves did not rise in the year after 0DTE growth. (A separate working paper finding dealer gamma predicts reversals was seen only as a search snippet and is not recorded.)
quote: we find no increase in frequency of such gap moves over the past year since the proliferation of 0DTE trading
title: Cboe: Much Ado About 0DTEs
